//: WHY this file exists: on 2026-07-29 a hand audit found SEVEN stale pins, including an EKS minor whose standard-support lapse silently 6x'd the control-plane bill and an External Secrets chart whose apiVersion had stopped being served. Every one of those would have arrived here as a PR months earlier. Renovate is the permanent fix for the class of problem; the audit was the symptom.

argocd.//: ArgoCD Application manifests carry chart pins in spec.sources[].targetRevision. Renovate's argocd manager reads those, which is where MOST of this repo's version surface lives.

packageRules.//: Group the observability stack. These charts are co-deployed and cross-reference each other's Services (loki-gateway, tempo:4317) and Grafana datasources, so reviewing them together beats seven isolated PRs.

Platform-critical controllers get their OWN PRs, never grouped. A bad bump to any of these can take the whole cluster down (the ALB controller's Service webhook blocks every Service create cluster-wide when it CrashLoops), so each must be revertible in isolation.

External Secrets majors have a history of removing served CRD apiVersions (v1beta1 dropped 2026-05-01). A major bump here REQUIRES a paired manifest rewrite, so flag it loudly rather than letting it look routine.
prBodyNotes: :warning: **Check served CRD apiVersions before merging.** ESO majors have removed apiVersion serving before. Run `scripts/crd_apiversion_gate.py` against the new chart — if `external-secrets.io/v1...` shows `served=false`, the manifests in `gitops/apps/external-secrets/` must be migrated in the SAME commit or ArgoCD fails with the opaque 'one or more synchronization tasks are not valid'.

packageRules.//: Terraform module majors (notably terraform-aws-modules/eks v20->v21) rename variables wholesale. Never auto-merge; always read the UPGRADE guide.
Digest/patch churn on the same chart line is noise; batch it weekly.

customManagers.//: The EKS Kubernetes minor lives in a Terraform variable DEFAULT, not a module pin, so no standard manager sees it -- which is precisely why 1.33 rotted past its standard-support date unnoticed. This regex manager tracks it against the EKS-supported releases so the next support deadline arrives as a PR instead of a surprise bill.
